title: AEM: Adaptive Entropy Modulation for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2605.00425v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the ability of large language model (LLM) agents to interact with environments and solve multi-turn tasks. However, effective agentic RL remains challenging: sparse outcome-only rewards provide limited guidance for assigning credit to individual steps within long interaction trajectories. Existing approaches often introduce dense intermediate supervision, such as process reward models or auxiliary self-supervised signals, which increases supervision and tuning complexity and may limit generalization across tasks and domains. We present AEM, a supervision-free credit assignment method that adaptively modulates entropy dynamics during RL training to improve the exploration-exploitation trade-off. Since in agentic RL the environment is typically affected by a complete response, rather than an individual token, our analysis lifts entropy dynamics from the token level to the response

translated_title: AEM：面向多轮智能体强化学习的自适应熵调制方法
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）显著提升了大语言模型（LLM）智能体与环境交互并解决多轮任务的能力。然而，有效的智能体强化学习仍然充满挑战：仅基于最终结果的稀疏奖励，对于在长交互轨迹中对各个步骤进行信用分配只能提供有限的指导。现有方法通常引入密集的中间监督，例如过程奖励模型或辅助自监督信号，这增加了监督与调参的复杂性，并可能限制跨任务、跨领域的泛化能力。我们提出了AEM，一种无需额外监督的信用分配方法，它在强化学习训练过程中自适应地调制熵的动态变化，以改善探索与利用之间的权衡。由于在智能体强化学习中，环境通常受完整响应（而非单个token）的影响，我们的分析将熵的动态从token层面提升到了响应层面（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 提出AEM，一种无需额外监督的信用分配方法，通过在响应层面自适应调制强化学习训练中的熵动态，改善多轮智能体强化学习中的探索-利用平衡。
en_tdlr: AEM is a supervision-free credit assignment method that adaptively modulates entropy dynamics at the response level during RL training, improving the exploration-exploitation trade-off in multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning.
